articles.title: Oktober inleds med global räntechock
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Oktober inleds med global räntechock
articles.body_text: Räntor i hela världen lyfter i takt med snabbt stigande marknadsräntor i USA. Arkivbild Dyrare bolån och börsfall kan bli tema framöver. Oktober har inletts med en räntechock på världsmarknaden, som tryckt upp ränteläget i alla stora ekonomier till de högsta nivåerna på årtionden. ”En brutal våg av försäljningar”, skriver Financial Times om hur marknadsaktörer dumpar amerikanska statsobligationer. Förutom finansiella problem för högt belånade hushåll och företag lägger höga marknadsräntor normalt en våt filt över riskaptiten, vilket kan skapa risk för kraftiga kursrörelser på börsen. I USA – ankaret på den globala räntemarknaden – är räntan på tioåriga statsobligationer nu uppe på 5,33 procent. Det är den högsta nivån sedan 2002. I Japan och Storbritannien är långa marknadsräntor samtidigt uppe på de högsta nivåerna sedan 1990-talet. Frankrike är också i blåsväder. Politisk oro och skakiga statsfinanser har tryckt upp gapet till tyska räntor till 1,31 procentenheter – det största gapet på nästan 15 år. De svenska långräntor har hängt med uppåt. Tioåringen är på 3,29 procent och för att hitta högre svenska marknadsräntor får man också gå tillbaka till 2011. Bedömare varnar för att ränteuppgångarna kommer att hålla i sig och kan fortsätta uppåt. Det är en strukturell och långvarig utveckling. Vi ser uppgången i räntor som en process där finansmarknaden försöker hitta en ny normal nivå, säger Steven Barrow på Standard Bank Advisory till nyhetbyrån Bloomberg. Högre råvaru- och energipriser, inflationsoro, handelskonflikter och skakiga statsfinanser – i en stark konjunktur med stabila tillväxtsignaler – har bäddat för utvecklingen.

articles.title: Kommunerna behöver vrida på vattenkranarna
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Kommunerna behöver vrida på vattenkranarna
articles.body_text: Det råder risk för vattenbrist i stora delar av landet. Arkivbild. Kommunerna behöver vrida på vattenkranarna Landets kommuner behöver öka investeringarna i vatten och avlopp. I fjol satsades 31 miljarder, nivån behöver upp till 37 miljarder kronor årligen för att klara behoven, enligt en branschrapport. Fram till 2040 handlar det om totalt 590 miljarder kronor. ”Vi behöver investera innan dagens utmaningar blir morgondagens kriser”, säger Pär Dalhielm, vd på Svenskt Vatten i en skriftlig kommentar. Kommunerna har redan blivit mycket bättre, med en fördubbling av investeringarna sedan 2019. Vattentaxorna har som en följd stigit kraftigt de senaste åren. Och för att kundernas vattenavgifter inte ska skena ytterligare krävs hjälp från staten, enligt Svenskt Vatten. "Nu är det dags för regeringen att skapa långsiktiga och moderna förutsättningar för att investeringarna ska kunna fortsätta”, säger Pär Dalhielm.

articles.title: Nytt elbilsrekord i Norge – total dominans
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Nytt elbilsrekord i Norge – total dominans
articles.body_text: Elbilar dominerar totalt på den norska nybilsmarknaden med en marknadsandel på nästan 99 procent. Arkivbild Nytt elbilsrekord i Norge – total dominans Elbilar slog nytt rekord i september när det gäller andel av nybilsförsäljningen i Norge, enligt branschorganisationen Opplysningsrådet for veitrafikken (OFV). Elbilarnas andel klättrade upp till 98,8 procent. Det kan jämföras med andelen på den svenska nybilsmarknaden, där elbilarnas andel i september var 49 procent. Bilförsäljningen i Norge lyfte samtidigt markant i september, upp 30,7 procent i årstakt. Tesla innehar tronen som mest säljande bilmärke i Norge med råge, med en marknadsandel på 26 procent i september. Det kan jämföras med Toyota på 7,1 procent och Volkswagen på 6,3 procent.

Om trenden ska hålla i sig förutsätter det långsiktiga spelregler, träffsäkra styrmedel som sänker trösklarna till elbil för fler hushåll men även en laddinfrastruktur som fungerar i vardagen”, säger Jessica Alenius, vd för Mobility Sweden i ett pressmeddelande.

articles.title: Klubbat – Helsingborg ska fånga in koldioxid
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Klubbat – Helsingborg ska fånga in koldioxid
articles.body_text: Helsingborg får en av Sveriges första CCS-anläggningar. Klubbat – Helsingborg ska fånga in koldioxid Filbornaverket i Helsingborg ska fånga in koldioxid. Bygget vid avfallsförbränningsanläggningen börjar redan i år och kostar 2,4 miljarder kronor. Öresundskraft har fattat det slutgiltiga investeringsbeslutet för satsningen, som går ut på att fånga in, transportera och lagra koldioxid, så kallad CCS. Tekniken har beskrivits som helt avgörande för att Helsingborg ska nå sina klimatmål. Koldioxiden – 200 000 ton årligen – ska mellanlagras i hamnen i Halmstad innan den transporteras vidare för slutlagring under Nordsjön, skriver Öresundskraft i ett pressmeddelande. Ett liknande bygge genomförs vid Värtaverket i Stockholm. EU innovationsfond och Energimyndigheten har varit med och finansierat under projektets gång.

articles.title: Publicistiska grunden för journalistik på TV4
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Hur fungerar den publicistiska grunden för nyhets- och samhällsjournalistik på TV4?
articles.body_text: Hur fungerar den publicistiska grunden för nyhets- och samhällsjournalistik på TV4? 9 januari 2024 ・ Uppdaterad: 15 augusti 2025 TV4:s nyhets- och samhällsbevakning ska vara i ögonhöjd med tittarna. Vi vill vara nära, personliga och inkluderande. För alla i hela Sverige. Vi ska vara trovärdiga och relevanta. Vi testar nya visuella former och utvecklar det rörliga berättandet. Vi är både snabba, och fördjupande. Vi ger plats för både humor och allvar. Vi påverkar och berör. Vi avslöjar maktmissbruk, och värnar pressfrihet och yttrandefrihet. Vi producerar Nyhetsmorgon, Nyhetsdagen, Efter fem och kvällsnyheter. Vi nyhetsrapporterar på tv4.se och fördjupar i kortdokumentärerna Nyheterna Story. Vår mångfaldigt prisbelönta redaktion Kalla Fakta granskar makt och missförhållanden. TV4:s nyhets- och samhällsbevakning sker ur ett riksperspektiv, med hela Sverige och världen som bevakningsområde. Vi har 17 rikskorrar på sex orter i Sverige. De finns i Luleå, Umeå, Östersund, Skövde, Göteborg och Malmö. Vi bevakar världen via utrikesreportrar, korrar och stringers. Vår journalistik vilar på respekt för alla människors lika värde, oavsett politisk åskådning, religion eller sexuell läggning. Det innebär att vi låter många röster komma till tals, även de som bär åsikter som inte nödvändigtvis delas av medarbetarna på redaktionen eller TV4. Men det kan också innebära att vi tar bort artikelkommentarer som kränker, eller till exempel avstår gäster i direktsändning där vi bedömer att risken är stor för missbruk av öppenheten. TV4:s nyhets- och samhällsjournalistik är oberoende och obunden. Den står fri från politiska partier, organisationer, och näringsliv. Vi har ingen ledarsida eller politisk färg. Innehållet på våra plattformar bedöms och värderas av redaktörer, producenter och av ansvarig utgivare före publicering. Vi följer grundlagen och skyddar våra källor när de önskar anonymitet. Om vi refererar uppgifter från andra medier redovisar vi vilka medier eller andra informationskällor det handlar om. Annars berättar vi hur vi själva tagit reda på informationen, dock alltid med största respekt för källskydd.

articles.summary: För första gången finns alla partiledare på Tiktok, samtidigt som nästan hälften av alla förstagångsväljare säger att de oftare tar del av politik på sociala medier än i tidningar, radio och tv. articles.summary: Teatrar och konserthus lockar allt oftare med olika sidoevenemang. articles.title: Wicknell Chivayo: Zimbabwean businessman and wife killed in helicopter crash
articles.summary: Chivayo was known for his lavish lifestyle, close ties to African presidents and lucrative government contracts.
articles.body_text: Prominent Zimbabwean businessman Wicknell Chivayo and his wife have been killed in a helicopter crash that left six people dead, his family have confirmed. The helicopter came down in the Marondera rural area, about 70km (43 miles) east of the capital, Harare, on Wednesday evening. Police said all six people on board died. Family spokesperson Herbert Chivayo confirmed the deaths of the businessman and his wife Lucy Muteke to state broadcaster ZBC, saying the family was devastated by the tragedy. Chivayo was known for his lavish lifestyle, close ties to some African presidents and lucrative government contracts that had repeatedly attracted scrutiny. He had denied allegations of wrongdoing linked to his business dealings. Police spokesperson Commissioner Paul Nyathi said the aircraft crashed at about 17:00 local time (15:00 GMT) and had six occupants, but authorities did not immediately identify all those on board. Two of the six were pilots, according to government officials. ZBC reported that the group was travelling from Gandami in Chikomba, where Chivayo and his wife were building a rural home, when the helicopter crashed at Kudenga Farm about 40 minutes after take-off. "We are at a loss for words after the tragic news," the family spokesperson, told the ZBC. The cause of the crash was not immediately known, and police said investigations were under way. Emergency services were sent to the scene on Wednesday evening. Earlier, government spokesman Nick Mangwana confirmed the crash, saying the helicopter was carrying "a prominent businessman, three other passengers and two pilots". "Current information indicates that there were no survivors in this crash," Mangwana posted on X. Chivayo was the managing director of Intratrek Zimbabwe and had built a high public profile through government contracts, philanthropy and displays of wealth on social media.

articles.title: California bans child marriage, a practice still legal in 32 US states
articles.summary: Gov Gavin Newsom called it a "long overdue measure to protect young Californians".
articles.body_text: California has officially banned child marriage, with Governor Gavin Newsom signing legislation to end the practice that is still legal in 32 US states. The new law, which will come into effect on 1 January, states people must be 18 to get married in the Golden State. Newsom called it a "long overdue measure to protect young Californians and minors". He signed the bill into law with Courtney Stodden, whose parents allowed her to marry a 50-year-old Hollywood actor when she was just 16. Stodden, who has been advocating to end the practice, called the change a "victory" and said survivors of child marriage should "never have been expected to carry this burden". Stodden said she would "keep fighting until children are protected from marriage in all 50 states". She was married to actor Doug Hutchison - known for roles in The Green Mile, A Time to Kill and I Am Sam - in 2011, spurring headlines internationally over the controversy and appearances on several reality programmes in the US, including the VH1 series Couples Therapy. Other survivors of child marriage also applauded the new law. "California has sent a clear message to the world today," Brittany Bee, a former child bride, told the BBC. "A message of hope for all children that they may be free from systemic violence. That they may choose their own path." Bee told the BBC she was wed at the age of 17 to escape an abusive home - only to then be allegedly abused by her adult husband. "I was just going from one prison to another," she explained. "People have the audacity to tell me that I made a choice - kids, they can't consent." Bee and other child marriage survivors have been working for years to have child marriages banned in California and across the United States. About a decade ago, the practice was still allowed across all US state but more and more states have been altering laws. California is the 18th to ban it since 2018.

articles.title: Swiss glaciers suffer 'disastrous' year of ice loss
articles.summary: Scientists say such rapid melting is no longer surprising given the pace of climate change.
articles.body_text: Swiss glaciers have suffered a near-record loss of ice in 2026, new data shows, as intense summer heatwaves take their toll on Alpine peaks. More than 5% of the country's remaining glacier ice has disappeared in the last 12 months, which scientists say is "extraordinary". They warn that such rapid melting is no longer a surprise given the pace of climate change, but it could threaten water supplies for farming, hydropower and transport in the decades ahead. The loss of glacier ice can also destabilise mountain slopes and increase the risk of landslides in some places - which can lead to flash flooding in extreme cases, as seen in Nepal in August. There were multiple factors involved in that event, which was triggered when a large area of bedrock and glacier ice collapsed. But scientists say long-term glacier thinning and the thawing of frozen ground likely raised the risks. The notable finding from this latest report is not so much that Swiss glaciers are shrinking - which is to be expected in our warming climate, driven primarily by fossil fuel emissions - but the sheer pace of melting. Until recently, glaciologists in the Alps considered 2% of ice lost in a single year to be "extreme". This year has seen an estimated 5.5% disappear. "It's really just disastrous," said Dr Matthias Huss, director of Glacier Monitoring Switzerland, which produced the report. Swiss glaciers started the summer in an already difficult place, covered by less snow than usual after a mild winter. And much of that snow disappeared quickly in the early and intense heatwaves of May and June , exposing the glacier ice below. Bare ice is darker and less reflective than fresh snow, so absorbs more of the Sun's energy.

articles.title: Balaghat, Madhya Pradesh: The children dying in India's remote tribal heartland
articles.summary: At least 32 children have died in India's Balaghat district since May amid outbreaks of measles and malaria.
articles.body_text: Warning: This article contains details some readers may find distressing At about 3am one morning in May, Bamita Markam began convulsing. The three-year-old had spent days with a high fever and angry red sores on her body. Her mother, Koushila, had first taken her to a doctor, who prescribed an ointment. Bamita seemed to recover, then became ill again. A faith healer, called to the house in Matla village, gave her syrups and tablets. Nothing worked. By dawn, Bamita was dead. "She cried a lot," Koushila recalls. "She convulsed all night." The family tried to make her drink water. At one point she vomited blood. They buried her in a jungle after midday. Bamita's death was one of at least 32 child deaths recorded since May in a cluster of remote villages in Balaghat district in India's Madhya Pradesh state, officials say. The victims ranged from babies just three or four months old to an 18-year-old, and most were Baiga, one of India's 75 "particularly vulnerable tribal groups" . Officials attribute the deaths to mainly measles and malaria, possibly aggravated by malnutrition and delays in treatment. They believe eight to 10 deaths were associated with measles, roughly another 10 with malaria, with several children suffering more than one infection. The precise cause of every death is less certain. "I have never seen an outbreak like this. My father was a two-term lawmaker, and I have served three terms, but neither of us has seen so many children die in such a short time," Sanjay Uikey, who has represented the area since 2013, told me. But disease is only part of the story. In remote, forested parts of Balaghat, where Maoist insurgency once took root, reaching a health centre can be a challenge in itself. In the monsoon, the terrain can make that journey harder. Paddy fields glow against red earth and low, forested hills. Narrow dirt tracks wind between fields and mud homes, often becoming slippery and impassable in heavy rain. The countryside is lush, but the homes are sparse. Most Baiga houses have low mud walls, rough timber and bamboo, and tiled or thatched roofs patched with plastic against the rain.

articles.title: China has cracked down on AI relationships. Is it ahead of the game?
articles.summary: Beijing has cracked down on AI chatbots that can replicate human relationships. Experts are asking if this is the right thing to do.
articles.body_text: In early 2024, a young man in the city of Huangshi, south-eastern China, reportedly posted a message on the Chinese version of TikTok, Douyin. The caption read: "Farewell to this world." Within minutes, the suicide prevention team at Douyin kicked into gear. The team, which is staffed 24 hours a day, shared the man's posts with five police stations in Huangshi. After geolocating one of his videos to a local park, police found him in emotional distress and intervened before he was able to take his own life. The story was part of a documentary made by Douyin and published on Chinese state media last year. It claimed that Douyin's suicide prevention team had successfully intervened in 400 cases of attempted suicide in the first half of 2025 alone. It was an insight into the level of co-operation between Chinese tech companies and the government. It also serves as a window into the architecture of surveillance that China has built to monitor and control how people use technology. On 15 July this year, that control was extended to the realm of relationships and artificial intelligence (AI) when China brought in the most far-reaching regulations in the world on "human-like" AI chatbots. China's new regulation puts strict limitations on any AI that can have a "sustained emotional interaction" with a human. US President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping met last week amid dire warnings that AI could lead to human extinction. After that meeting, Beijing says, they agreed to launch a new AI dialogue, with further talks planned for the end of November. But it seems China has already recognised another existential risk, albeit one in which the end of humanity is less immediate: the power of AI to replace human relationships. Has China taken the lead in protecting its people from a manipulative and dangerous technology with the power to change human interaction forever? Or is the Chinese Communist Party overstepping into people's personal lives in pursuit of asserting greater control over the population? Until this regulation came in, the reach of AI companions in China was vast. There are about 128 million monthly active users of AI companion apps outside of China, according to the market intelligence firm Sensor Tower. Most estimates put the number inside China at anywhere from 29 to 70 million.

articles.title: Tennessee death row inmate Christa Pike survives execution attempt after two injections
articles.summary: Killer Christa Pike's lawyer says she is being given "life-saving measures" in hospital after two syringes of pentobarbital.
articles.body_text: Tennessee death row inmate Christa Pike has been taken to hospital after an attempt to execute her by two lethal injections failed, her lawyer says. Her legal team filed an emergency motion to halt the convicted murderer's execution as it was happening, saying: "Ms Pike has lost consciousness and still has a heartbeat and is audibly snoring." One of her attorneys told the BBC that Pike, 50, was now "being provided life-saving measures" in hospital after two syringes of pentobarbital had been administered. Pike was sentenced to death in 1996 for the murder of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer. Her execution was the subject of a last-minute legal battle. This culminated in the US Supreme Court allowing the lethal injections to go ahead. Pike was 18 when she and her then-boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp, beat, tortured and killed 19-year-old Slemmer, whom they had met at a job training camp for troubled teens. Slemmer's mother May Martinez was among those who wanted the execution to take place. Speaking to NBC News after Wednesday evening's events, she said: "It was a mess." The attempted execution took place at Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville at about 20:00 local time (01:00 GMT on Thursday). Pike was given two doses of the chemical pentobarbital, and the curtain in the witness room was closed twice, the AP news agency reported. Media were at some point asked to leave, the news agency said. AP added that Tennessee's execution protocol calls for a secondary set of drug syringes in case the person being put to death does not die after the first set. But it does not spell out what happens if the subject is alive after the second set. In a statement reported by US media, Tennessee Governor Bill Lee said he had ordered "a comprehensive, third-party review to determine exactly what occurred". He said the year's last remaining execution would not go ahead as planned.

articles.title: Tiny image sparks big backlash in Nikon photo contest
articles.summary: Dr Ning Xu denies he broke the rules of Nikon's annual Small World In Motion contest.
articles.body_text: The winning entry of a prestigious scientific photography competition is being re-evaluated following criticism from other scientists that it was made with AI. Nikon's annual Small World In Motion contest accepts photos and video taken using powerful microscopes, and has run annually for the last 15 years. The winner was a short video submitted by Dr Ning Xu, a researcher at Tsinghua University in China, which claims to be footage of tiny, hair-like structures called cilia moving inside the airways of a child with a rare disease. Xu did not respond to the BBC's request for comment, but has posted online denying he broke the competition rules. In a response to a post by Nikon on LinkedIn , he did not dispute using AI within the image processing but said he remained within the rules of the contest. "AI was not used to generate the experimental movie, the cilia, or their motion," he said. Xu's video is artificially brightly coloured - common in microscopy and permitted in the contest - which is usually done manually using stains and dyes on the sample itself. He accepted AI was used "to distinguish and visualize features in the reconstructed grayscale images". But the challenges made by other scientists include claims that the video contains shapes and movements which did not fit with normal cell structures or behaviours, and that the cilia seemed to be too big. Commenting on Nikon's social media post, Edward Phelps, associate professor at Florida University, observed some of the structures "pop in and out of existence" and the cilia "appear from nowhere". Meanwhile PhD student Ian Donovan from UT Southwestern Medical Centre said the source image appeared to contain a distinctive watermark indicating it had been AI generated. Additionally, two former competition judges said they also had concerns about whether the image was real.

articles.title: Putin shows no sign of stopping the war as Russia doubles down on Ukraine
articles.summary: A foreign policy speech by the Russian president will be keenly watched, but all signs point to the full-scale invasion continuing.
articles.body_text: When Vladimir Putin arrived to address Russia's parliament on Wednesday, a warm welcome was guaranteed. "The Special Election Operation", as one Russian newspaper dubbed last month's legislative vote , has produced a State Duma even more pro-Putin than anything before it. The ruling party, United Russia, now has more MPs than ever. It allows the Kremlin to claim it has been handed a huge mandate from the Russian people. Are there any signs he is prepared to halt what he calls the special military operation? Or should we brace for further escalation in Ukraine and in tensions with Europe? On Thursday I'll be watching to see whether Russia's leader sheds light on his plans during an appearance at the Valdai Discussion Club in Moscow. Traditionally the president's speech at this annual foreign policy forum provides insight into Putin's world view. Right now, everything points to Putin continuing Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine: despite his country's huge battlefield losses to date and the damage being done to Russia's economy. Putin's speeches and statements suggest he remains confident that Russia can secure a military victory. Judging by what is being reported in Russian media, Moscow is encouraged by the shortage of air defence missiles in Ukraine, as well as the expectation that Russian strikes this winter will increase pressure on Ukrainians. Kyiv has spoken of its difficulty in shooting down Russia's ballistic missiles and new jet-powered drones, which have been targeting Ukraine every day. The Kremlin has made no secret of the fact it wants European states to slash their military and financial backing for Ukraine: the kind of support Moscow says is prolonging the war - or, rather, getting in the way of a Russian victory. To achieve this, Western officials believe Russia has been sending not so subtle signals. They accuse Moscow of waging an escalating hybrid war on European countries through cyber-attacks, acts of sabotage, and Russian drones violating European airspace. In Germany, a drone carrying an explosive device was found close to Ukrainian cargo planes at Leipzig airport.

articles.title: Annapurna Circuit: Trekkers helicoptered off mountains as more deadly landslides hit Nepal
articles.summary: A month after mass catastrophic flooding, around 30 people have died in landslides and heavy rain.
articles.body_text: Another wave of landslides and heavy rain has killed about 30 people in Nepal, as the Himalayan nation reels from August's catastrophic flooding that left 1,400 dead and thousands more missing. The national disaster management authority says more than 1,900 families have been affected since late last week with more than 240 homes damaged. Roads, buildings and bridges have been swept away. Hundreds of trekkers on the Annapurna Circuit - crucial to Nepal's economy - have had to cut short their hikes to get to safety. Many have been helicoptered out of the districts of Manang and Mustang, from a hiking circuit that usually takes up to three weeks to complete. Communities in several parts of Nepal are mourning loved ones. Speaking from a damp, blue tent in Battar, a town north-west of Kathmandu, Buti Tamang told BBC Nepali: "We used to live in a hut, but now there is nothing. We have lost so many of our relatives." "Now it is raining and the tent leaks, so we've been facing a difficult situation. We have nowhere to go," said Ramesh Ghale, who also had to flee his home. Several trekkers and their guides say their journeys back down the mountains have been treacherous, taking up to three or four days and requiring them to pass collapsed roads and swept-away bridges. Jake Stacy, a 21-year-old from Suffolk, found himself stranded with his guide in Yak Kharka, upper Manang, due to heavy snowfall last week and decided not to continue to the Thorang La pass, the highest point of the circuit. "We made our own paths on mountain slopes," he said, after returning to base camp in Pokhara on Tuesday night. "It was quite steep and we were clambering because there was river below… It was very muddy and very wet. "Many trekkers were helicoptered out," he added. Australian Andrew Graham and his guide Prem KC said they had to cross more than 15 landslides after they decided to return from Manang village. "A few of them were quite dangerous, the residual risks have grown now."

articles.title: Too early to say if Iran involved in Dubai-Tel Aviv flight attack, Israeli PM says
articles.summary: A pilot who stabbed another pilot on an Israel-bound plane is being investigated in Saudi Arabia, Benjamin Netanyahu says.
articles.body_text: It is too early to say if Iran had any involvement in an attack by a pilot who stabbed another pilot and tried to take over a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv, Israel's prime minister has said. The Flydubai plane plunged more than 17,000ft (5,200m) two hours into its journey on Wednesday, before passengers and crew overpowered the attacker and retook control to land safely. The stabbed pilot, Indian national Captain Smit Machchhar, is in hospital in a stable condition, and has been hailed a "true hero" by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. One passenger, Yaniv Hayun, described how he put the attacker, who was trying to disable the plane, in a chokehold before other passengers helped pin him down. The alleged attacker, who was arrested in Saudi Arabia, is expected to be transferred to the United Arab Emirates, where the plane took off from, Netanyahu told Fox News. Asked whether there was any indication as of now of Iran's involvement, he replied: "It's too early to say". He added that the pilot was "now being investigated in Saudi Arabia". US President Donald Trump said he had spoken with Netanyahu following the incident, saying it seemed as though the attacker was "perhaps a terrorist" or there were other reasons behind the attack. Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz has also called it an "attempted jihadist terror attack", without giving any details. Netanyahu told CNN Israel did not have any warning or advance intelligence about the incident on the plane, which was flying 174 people to Israel. Flydubai's flight FZ1073 took off from Dubai International Airport in the UAE at 03:05 GMT (07:05 local time), en route to Ben Gurion Airport. Two hours later, the 17,000ft drop in altitude was reported on the plane tracking website Flightradar24 and minutes later the plane signalled an emergency code - squawk 7700 - before switching it to a squawk 7500 code reporting a hijacking. Around 20 minutes after these codes were signalled, the plane started its manual descent for landing into Saudi Arabia. Less than an hour later, the plane returned to squawk 7700.

articles.title: Six smugglers jailed for manslaughter over worst Channel small boats disaster
articles.summary: Thirty-one migrants died when their boat went down in November 2021. The trial found that the guilty men were part of two smuggling networks.
articles.body_text: Six people traffickers have been found guilty in France of causing the deaths of 31 migrants in the worst ever small-boat accident in the Channel. At the end of a four-week trial in Paris, the six were convicted of "involuntary homicide" and given prison terms of between six and 10 years. Seven others were given lesser sentences of up to four years, and one person was found not guilty. The boat went down early in the morning on 24 November 2021 after sending distress calls to French and British coastguards. The dead, including a child of seven, were mainly Iraqi Kurds but also included Afghans, Egyptians and Iranian Kurds. Only two men survived. The charge sheet said the migrants had been put to sea from the French coast in a boat "that was of poor quality, uncertified, unsuitable for navigation at sea, overloaded, and without correct life jackets". The trial established that the guilty men were members of two separate networks – one of which was Iraqi Kurd, the other Afghan – that co-operated to organise the cross-channel journey and bring migrants to the meeting point. Unusually the court was attended at the start by several family members, who came to France from Iraqi Kurdistan and gave moving testimony about how the victims came to be on board the boat. Speaking after the verdict, their lawyer Matthieu Chirez said the decision "comes as a relief for all the civil plaintiffs because it confirms the penal responsibility of the traffickers". He said the trial had "humanised the families of victims". One family member, Zana Marmand Muhammed, told the court how his younger brother Twana had "wanted to go to England to find a job and because the geopolitical situation with us is dangerous. No-one in the family wanted him to leave, but we could not dissuade him." Nabi Mustafa Mina, the father of Zanyar who was 19 when he died, told of how he tried to dissuade his son from leaving. "I said I would help him to get married, I would give him my house, I would divide my salary in two. But no, he said he wanted a better life, that he would get by somehow. I ran out of arguments," he said. The family-members explained how they had paid a deposit at a bank in Iraqi Kurdistan and then followed their loved ones' progress through Turkey, Italy and then France. In one of the last messages from Twana, he posted a picture of himself at the Eiffel Tower.

articles.title: Russia launches largest attack on Ukraine energy infrastructure since spring
articles.summary: In total 11 regions of the country were attacked overnight, with residential buildings and railways also targeted, the Ukrainian PM says.
articles.body_text: Russia has launched the largest attack on Ukraine's energy infrastructure since the spring, primarily targeting Kyiv and the surrounding region, Ukraine's Prime Minister has said. At least five people were killed in overnight attacks across the country, including a child in the Kyiv region, Serhiy Koretskyi said. The strikes also impacted people's power supplies, with Ukraine's biggest private energy firm DTEK saying power to 8,000 homes had been restored following "a difficult night" for the capital. The Russian defence ministry said one of its targets was the Trypilska power station, the largest supplier of electricity to Kyiv. The operator confirmed damage to the plant. Koretskyi wrote on Telegram: "Since the summer, there has effectively not been a single day without enemy attacks on our energy infrastructure. "However, a mass and combined attack of this scale has occurred for the first time since the end of the last heating season." Ukraine has been expecting another protracted Russian assault on the country's energy grid. It has happened every winter so far since Russia's full-scale invasion began in 2022. In total, 11 regions of the country were attacked overnight, with residential buildings, social infrastructure, civilian enterprises and railways also targeted, Koretskyi said. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said there had been strikes on critical infrastructure in the Zhytomyr, Mykolaiv, Kirovohrad and Rivne regions. On Wednesday, some households in the Kyiv, Dnipropetrovsk, Donetsk, Sumy and Kharkiv regions remained without power, Ukraine's energy ministry said. State-owned grid operator Ukrenergo advised residents not to use powerful electrical appliances between the hours of 10:00 and 16:00 local time as electricity supplies were lower than usual. In Kyiv, people woke to find the city blanketed by thick, acrid smoke after a night punctuated by the sound of explosions. An air raid alert was still on and the distant sound of air defence gunfire echoed through the murky atmosphere.

articles.title: Last UK and US troops leave Iraq as anti-Islamic State mission ends
articles.summary: The withdrawal of coalition forces, under a deal agreed two years ago, was a key demand of the Iraqi government.
articles.body_text: The last British and American troops have left Iraq after a military presence of more than a decade in the country. The exit of the remaining UK military personnel - around 100 - from Irbil, in the northern Kurdistan region, was co-ordinated over recent weeks with US forces, who also departed on Wednesday. It follows an agreement between the US and the Iraqi government, signed two years ago, to withdraw foreign troops by the end of this month. British and US forces have been present in Iraq since 2014, as part of the international coalition to help defeat the extremist Islamic State (IS) group. Their departure brings the mission, known as Operation Inherent Resolve, to an end. Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi said the end of the coalition's mission marked "Iraq's transition to a phase in which it assumes full responsibility for its security and stability". Iraq is set to hold four "Sovereignty Days" as a national holiday to mark the withdrawal. "Following more than a decade of operations, training and capacity building, Iraqi Security Forces (ISF) and the Kurdish Peshmerga have secured the enduring territorial defeat of Daesh in Iraq and are now well placed to take primary responsibility for the country's security," the UK Ministry of Defence (MoD) said in a statement, referring to IS by an Arabic acronym. "With these objectives achieved, Iraq and its international partners can begin a new chapter focused on enduring security co-operation under Iraqi leadership." US President Donald Trump celebrated the withdrawal, calling it a "victory for the United States, a victory for Iraq, and a decisive victory over ISIS". Writing in a Truth Social post, the president added: "It has been a long time, with very bad decision-making that got us involved in this quagmire in the first place, but soon, that will be part of History." Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell also said the coalition's departure from Irbil marked "the successful conclusion of the military mission that defeated [IS] in Iraq". He added: "The primary responsibility for addressing Iraq's remaining security challenges, including [IS] remnants and Iran-aligned militias that undermine Iraqi sovereignty and regional stability, now rests with the government of Iraq."

articles.title: What we know about stabbing on Flydubai flight to Israel
articles.summary: A pilot has been arrested and is being questioned after another pilot was stabbed, officials say.
articles.body_text: A flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv was diverted to Saudi Arabia on Wednesday after one pilot stabbed the other and "apparently tried to crash the plane", Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said. The pilot was arrested and is being questioned by Saudi authorities, Netanyahu added. The stabbed pilot, identified as Indian national Capt Smit Machchhar, was taken to hospital after the flight landed and later called a "hero" by the Israeli prime minister. Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz has called the incident an "attempted jihadist terror attack". The BBC is yet to receive official statements from police, emergency services, or investigators regarding any motive. Flydubai's flight FZ1073 took off from Dubai International Airport in the United Arab Emirates at 03:05 GMT (07:05 local time) en route to Ben-Gurion Airport in Israel. The flight was carrying at least 150 people, with Netanyahu saying "almost all" passengers were Israeli. Data from flight tracking website Flightrader24 shows a rapid descent for the plane over Saudi Arabia around two and a half hours after take-off, dropping more than 17,000 feet (over 5,000m) in less than two minutes at around 05:21. Minutes later, the plane signalled an emergency code - squawk 7700 - before switching it to a squawk 7500 code reporting a hijacking. At 05:40, the plane - which had briefly entered Jordanian airspace - looped back into Saudi Arabia, where it later started its manual descent for landing. Less than an hour later, the plane returned to squawk 7700. Initial local media reports cited Israeli officials as saying a fight had broken out between two pilots. But, speaking on Wednesday following the incident, Netanyahu confirmed later reports that one pilot had stabbed the other before "apparently trying to crash" the plane.

articles.summary: Este lunes 28 de septiembre desde las 3:45 p.m., Keiko Fujimori, presidenta del Perú, realizará un anuncio en materia laboral en una ceremonia que se llevará a cabo en Palacio de Gobierno.
articles.body_text: Este lunes 28 de septiembre desde las 3:45 p.m., Keiko Fujimori, presidenta del Perú, realizará un anuncio en materia laboral en una ceremonia que se llevará a cabo en Palacio de Gobierno. Uno de los puntos que la mandataria abordará será la aprobación del primer tramo del sueldo mínimo. Como se recuerda, Fujimori anunció el incremento de la Remuneración Mínima Vital (RMV) a S/1.300. La mandataria estará acompañada de Luis Galarreta, presidente del Consejo de Ministros. Además, la ceremonia contará con la participación de Juan Sheput, ministro de Trabajo y Promoción del Empleo y el titular del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas, Elmer Cuba. Cabe señalar que el ministro de Trabajo, Juan Sheput, sostuvo que el primer alza de la RMV, de unos S/100, se aplicaría entre octubre y noviembre de este año, mientras que el segundo incremento, de S/70, en el siguiente semestre.

articles.title: Perú Sub 20 Odesur: el bronce es una buena noticia pero ahora, ¿cuál es la gran tarea de los clubes?
articles.summary: La selección peruana Sub 20, con gol de Cari y autogol de Orellana, consiguió el bronce en los Odesur tras vencer 2-1 a Chile y dejó una noticia que el fútbol peruano necesitaba. Pero el verdadero desafío empieza ahora: acompañar a estos jóvenes y exigir a los clubes que les den real competencia
articles.body_text: Más que ilusión, efímera y por eso mismo impredecible, la selección peruana Sub 20 que acaba de obtener el bronce en los Odesur, me provoca alegría. El rostro de los muchachos, una cierta paz. Hecho de retazos, con clubes en ruinas y una Liga 1 que se juega también en los juzgados, el fútbol peruano tiene por fin una buena noticia. Fue 2-1 sobre Chile, contra quien no hay que jugar, solo ganar. Y aunque somos -mea culpa- usualmente ingratos con ellos, pocas veces cubrimos sus entrenamientos, no entendemos los procesos y mucho menos las carencias y, sobre todo, les pedimos respuestas de adultos cuando apenas han terminado el colegio, su optimismo es tan colectivo que en su mesa de festejos hay sitio para todos. No alcanza, sin embargo, con felicitarlos y publicar sus fotos radiantes. Hace falta acompañarlos -la verdadera prueba de fuego es el Sub 20 de enero- y exigir: es escalofriante que ningún jugador de esta selección sea titular en un equipo de Primera -ni siquiera la figura del equipo, Piero Cari, olvidado en Matute-, y que solo sea Sporting Cristal quien realmente proteja una política de exposición y crecimiento de su cantera: Jair Moretti, Josémaría Mellan -la personalidad que tiene-, Duham Ballumbrosio o Gerson Castillo, cuatro megatitulares del equipo de Thiago Kosloski, tienen minutos en la Liga 1 y, en su postura, su juego, su físico, se nota. La Sub 17 de Oré, los medallistas de Nanjing y ahora ellos. Tres buenas campañas de menores en veinte años no alcanza y no alcanzará si se repiten los mismos errores: clubes de corto plazo, dirigentes débiles y reporteros que nos metemos hasta su desayuno. Bastante sólido en defensa, solidario en el medio y quizá demasiado cuidadoso contra rivales que se presentan superiores -el partido contra Argentina de semis- el equipo peruano se suma a la legión de ganadores de estos Odesur. Que la alegría dure hoy y mañana todo sea triple exigencia. Sobre todo para los ciegos clubes.

articles.title: Perú Sub 20 Odesur: el bronce es una buena noticia pero ahora, ¿cuál es la gran tarea de los clubes?
articles.summary: La selección peruana Sub 20, con gol de Cari y autogol de Orellana, consiguió el bronce en los Odesur tras vencer 2-1 a Chile y dejó una noticia que el fútbol peruano necesitaba. Pero el verdadero desafío empieza ahora: acompañar a estos jóvenes y exigir a los clubes que les den real competencia
articles.body_text: Más que ilusión, efímera y por eso mismo impredecible, la selección peruana Sub 20 que acaba de obtener el bronce en los Odesur, me provoca alegría. El rostro de los muchachos, una cierta paz. Hecho de retazos, con clubes en ruinas y una Liga 1 que se juega también en los juzgados, el fútbol peruano tiene por fin una buena noticia. Fue 2-1 sobre Chile, contra quien no hay que jugar, solo ganar. Y aunque somos -mea culpa- usualmente ingratos con ellos, pocas veces cubrimos sus entrenamientos, no entendemos los procesos y mucho menos las carencias y, sobre todo, les pedimos respuestas de adultos cuando apenas han terminado el colegio, su optimismo es tan colectivo que en su mesa de festejos hay sitio para todos. No alcanza, sin embargo, con felicitarlos y publicar sus fotos radiantes. Hace falta acompañarlos -la verdadera prueba de fuego es el Sub 20 de enero- y exigir: es escalofriante que ningún jugador de esta selección sea titular en un equipo de Primera -ni siquiera la figura del equipo, Piero Cari, olvidado en Matute-, y que solo sea Sporting Cristal quien realmente proteja una política de exposición y crecimiento de su cantera: Jair Moretti, Josémaría Mellan -la personalidad que tiene-, Duham Ballumbrosio o Gerson Castillo, cuatro megatitulares del equipo de Thiago Kosloski, tienen minutos en la Liga 1 y, en su postura, su juego, su físico, se nota. La Sub 17 de Oré, los medallistas de Nanjing y ahora ellos. Tres buenas campañas de menores en veinte años no alcanza y no alcanzará si se repiten los mismos errores: clubes de corto plazo, dirigentes débiles y reporteros que nos metemos hasta su desayuno. Bastante sólido en defensa, solidario en el medio y quizá demasiado cuidadoso contra rivales que se presentan superiores -el partido contra Argentina de semis- el equipo peruano se suma a la legión de ganadores de estos Odesur. Que la alegría dure hoy y mañana todo sea triple exigencia. Sobre todo para los ciegos clubes.

articles.title: Google releases Gemini 4 Argon, called its most powerful model yet | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Google has released its latest Gemini model, marketing it as a workhorse for coding and cybersecurity work.
articles.body_text: Google parent company Alphabet has launched Gemini 4 Argon, a new AI model built to handle a variety of tasks such as coding, research, and writing. But it’s cybersecurity that Gemini 4 Argon is supposed to have a particular knack for, according to Google. Argon is only being rolled out to a select group of the company’s cyber partners through its Fairwind Program, Google’s security initiative. The model was trained specifically for defensive cyber work, and the company says it can “autonomously find, validate, and patch critical software vulnerabilities.” Argon is also said to be good at coding and engineering, with the company noting that its own staff have already been using the model for their daily work, including debugging and codebase migrations. Google also touts Argon’s ability to parse visuals — whether that’s analyzing the contents of long videos or charts. “Built to sustain deep reasoning across complex, long-horizon workflows, Argon is fundamentally changing the way we work and build at Google,” the company said in a blog post Wednesday. Top AI labs have rushed to release increasingly powerful models, attempting to outdo each other even as those very same firms warn that AI could spin out of control. Not long ago, OpenAI released Astra — which it hailed as its best model yet. Earlier this year, Anthropic’s Fable was also released with similar rhetoric from the company. Firms have done their best to market their services as superior to their competitors. In its blog, Google claims that Argon scored significantly higher than OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra and Anthropic’s Fable and Opus models across a variety of AI benchmarks. It cites Vals — an increasingly popular AI benchmarking startup — to show that Argon is currently the leading model on the company’s AI model index. Once considered “ behind ” in the AI race, Google has recently enjoyed success with Gemini. The company announced in August that its app had over a billion users per month , a metric that makes it competitive with OpenAI, which also recently announced that ChatGPT had reached a billion monthly users. articles.title: The Pentagon taps Elon Musk and Palmer Luckey to help decide what the military should do next | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth just launched a 120-day study on the future of warfare, led by Elon Musk, Palmer Luckey, and Newt Gingrich, and while it makes sense given their ties to the administration, critics could point out that Musk's and Luckey's companies already sell the kinds of technology the study is likely to recommend.
articles.body_text: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth used a “ State of the Force ” address on Wednesday to launch a new effort to study how war may be fought as tech advances rapidly. It’s being called Project Meridian. Elon Musk, Anduril founder Palmer Luckey, and former House Speaker Newt Gingrich will co-lead the project. They’ll be joined by others from fields such as academia and policy, all working under the direction of Defense Department CTO Emil Michael. Their job is to “study the battlefields of the future” and the “weapons and technologies warfighters” may use on them, said Hegseth in a letter announcing the project. The team (it is unclear how many people will be on it) will have 120 days to submit its findings and propose “actionable solutions to start developing, testing, and fielding” advanced technology meant to keep America a dominant military power, per Hegseth. Hegseth also announced an Autonomous Warfare Command on Wednesday to speed up the development and deployment of autonomous systems and drones. One curious detail in the Pentagon’s announcement is that the study will come through a partner organization , but the announcement does not say what that organization is or who leads it. After TechCrunch reached out to the Defense Department for comment, the department referred us to a press release , saying it had “nothing further to provide beyond the Secretary’s comments.” Musk’s and Luckey’s involvement is hardly surprising. Musk, in particular, has reportedly renewed close ties with the administration and recently had lunch with the president — alongside other top AI leaders — to discuss the future of AI . The project seemingly marks his first official return to the administration’s fold since he left the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) last year. Musk’s SpaceX launches satellites for the U.S. government and operates a satellite network that supports national defense and security missions. Luckey’s defense tech company, Anduril, meanwhile, creates autonomous military systems and drones and was recently awarded government contracts to produce long-range missiles and semi-autonomous fighter aircraft and to supply hardware and integration for the Army’s mobile intelligence system . The Trump administration has made advanced military technology a priority, in both development and purchasing, and has looked to Silicon Valley-approved companies to help make this happen. Critics could argue that putting Musk and Luckey on Project Meridian directly aligns with their business interests, since they would be trying to find solutions their companies already sell. articles.title: Factory CEO just accused his VC board adviser of spying for Cognition | TechCrunch
articles.summary: VC Chris Degnan and former board adviser to Factory AI has taken a job as chief revenue officer for competitor Cognition -- and everyone is arguing on X about it.
articles.body_text: Matan Grinberg, co-founder and CEO of the AI coding startup Factory, said in a post on X on Wednesday that he fired VC Chris Degnan from his role as a board adviser. Grinberg alleges that Degnan shared confidential information with Factory’s biggest competitor, Cognition. Two hours after Grinberg’s post, Degnan announced on both X and LinkedIn that he had joined Cognition as its chief revenue officer. He also subsequently refuted Grinberg’s allegations, saying in a separate X post that he wasn’t fired but resigned when he told Grinberg he was taking the job. Degnan was Snowflake’s first sales hire and later spent 11 years as the data company’s chief revenue officer. For the past five months, he has been a partner with RPT Partners, a Newport Beach, California, investor in Factory. Degnan is also a go-to-market adviser to startups at the much bigger venture firm Iconiq , a role that dates back to October of last year. Three-year-old, San Francisco-based Factory is an agentic coding startup whose AI agents can carry out programming tasks largely on their own. The company raised $200 million at a $5 billion valuation this month from Khosla Ventures, Blackstone, Sequoia Capital, Insight Partners, and others. Its customers include Nvidia, Blackstone, Royal Bank of Canada, Palo Alto Networks, Adobe, and T-Mobile. Grinberg said he sees Cognition, the maker of the Devin coding agent, as his biggest competitor. Cognition raised another $2 billion at a $48 billion valuation earlier this month , and counts Mercedes-Benz, NASA, Goldman Sachs, and Citi as customers. Grinberg said on X that Degnan had earlier acknowledged having a “casual” conversation with a Cognition executive but had assured Grinberg that he had no interest in working for the competitor. According to Grinberg, Degnan said he had “made too much money” and was “too lazy to go work for Cognition,” which Grinberg said he “trusted and believed.” On Monday, however, Degnan apparently disclosed that he had actually been in ongoing talks with Cognition. This caused Grinberg to grow concerned about how much confidential information Degnan had about Factory, and how much he had shared and might share in the future with his new employer. He says he fired Degnan as a board adviser on Tuesday, writing: For weeks, while he sat in our board meetings and advised our leadership team, he was also confiding with executives of our largest competitor. Chris was subject to confidentiality obligations in connection with his work with Factory. We do not know the extent of the information he shared, but it puts his timely questions about our product roadmap and what the parity gap involves into a new light. But Degnan disputes that account as well. He says the last Factory board meeting he attended was weeks before he had “ever spoken” to Cognition and that he hasn’t shared confidential information. Degnan also says that when he told Grinberg that he was resigning to take the role at Cognition, Grinberg offered him a full-time job at Factory, which he declined. Really disappointed to see this. Here are the facts: -You did not terminate me. I resigned from my advisor position on Monday and told you I was going to Cognition. In response, you asked me to consider a full time role at Factory. I told you I wasn’t interested. -You claim… Degnan’s post announcing his new job at Cognition doesn’t mention Factory. Very notably, it does say that RPT Partners and the firm’s managing partner, Chad Peets, will now be working with Cognition. “I am thrilled that Chad and the RPT team will be working closely with me in our pursuit of building a generational company,” Degnan wrote.

articles.title: Hackers stole millions of US military personnel records during months-long data breach | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The Department of Defense notified millions of current and former U.S. military personnel that their personal information had been stolen in a months-long breach.
articles.body_text: The U.S. government is reportedly alerting millions of current and former U.S. military service members and staff that their personal information was stolen during a months-long breach of the Pentagon’s personnel records, the latest in a spate of thefts involving federal workers’ data in recent months. A data breach notification from the Defense Manpower Data Center (DMDC) shared on Reddit says that several unauthorized users exploited a security vulnerability in an unspecified file-sharing system over several months between October 2025 and mid-July 2026. The breach exposed personally identifiable information, including Social Security numbers, alongside a person’s name, date of birth, sex, race, and other information about their military service. The notice says that the personnel records were unencrypted. According to CNN and Federal News Network , a Pentagon official said the breach affects about 2.8 million living people, and close to 300,000 people who are deceased. The U.S. military has 1.3 million active service members as of March. The DMDC may not be widely known to the general public, but serves as one of the Department of Defense’s records-keeping units. The DMDC maintains over 60 million records for U.S. military and civilian staff and their family members to help determine benefits and entitlements, such as healthcare and retirement. The unit also provides a critical service as the military’s “leading identity management provider,” which links active service members, employees, and contractors to credentials, such as smart cards and passwords. These are used to access Pentagon computer systems, buildings, and bases. “We make sure that the right people get access and the wrong people don’t: security of identity information is paramount,” the DMDC’s website reads. The Department of Defense, which oversees the DMDC, said it does not have any indication that the information was misused, but did not say how it reached that conclusion. TechCrunch contacted a Pentagon spokesperson to ask if officials had any communications from the hackers, whose identities are not known, but we did not hear back. This is the latest major breach of federal workers’ personal information in recent months, following a recent breach at the FBI earlier in September attributed to the ShinyHunters hacking group. The hackers told TechCrunch that they had taken the personal information of most of the FBI’s agents and staffers, including applicants. The breach has been billed as a “counterintelligence disaster” amid the risks that a foreign government could obtain and use the information to profile, target, or coerce federal workers into handing over sensitive information. The ShinyHunters hackers have said that they will not publicly release the stolen FBI data . Both breaches involving the FBI and the DMDC mirror similar thefts of government personnel records in the past. In 2015, a breach of the U.S. government’s human resources department, known as the Office of Personnel Management, was broadly attributed to China. The theft allowed the hackers to steal the private records of more than 22 million U.S. government employees, many of whom had security clearances. Did you receive a notice about this data breach? articles.title: DoorDash's drone strategy started on the ground | TechCrunch
articles.summary: DoorDash unveiled the six-propeller aircraft that will be used in its new drone delivery business at its annual Dash Forward 2026 event.
articles.body_text: When DoorDash set out to build a drone delivery business , it started with the tricky logistics that happen on the ground before it looked up. The autonomous drone came last, according to the company, which unveiled its new six-propeller aircraft at its annual Dash Forward 2026 event on Wednesday. Before DoorDash worked on the aircraft, the company focused on ground infrastructure, including loading systems, how food would be handed off from a restaurant’s kitchen, and packaging. DoorDash Labs, the R&D team that built its autonomous sidewalk delivery bot Dot, created the drone delivery service now called DoorDash Air. The same team also developed the underlying software, called the Autonomous Delivery Platform (ADP), to handle the coordination challenges in deliveries handled by humans, sidewalk delivery bots, and now drones. The ADP software uses smart routing, incorporating factors like weather, flight range, and ground traffic to narrow down which orders actually make sense to send by air. The company’s systems-first strategy for its DoorDash Air business aligns with its strengths. DoorDash isn’t a hardware company, but it is sitting on 13 years of user data from the merchant and customer sides of the business. (DoorDash has previously disclosed that more than 500,000 restaurants are on its delivery marketplace.) The company says it sized the whole DoorDash Air system around its historical order data, including how much orders weigh and how far they typically travel. “We didn’t start with a drone and ask what would fit,” Harrison Shih, who heads up DoorDash Air, said in a statement. “We started with what people order and how local businesses actually operate, then built the entire system from there.” DoorDash announced plans in July to launch the drone delivery business after receiving a Part 135 air carrier certification from the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration. The certification allows the company to legally operate a commercial drone delivery service in the United States. The drone, which has six slow-spinning propellers mounted at the ends of its arms, is equipped with a winch to pick up, carry, and drop off packages. DoorDash said it plans to kick off early pilot deliveries in Northern California with partners including Chipotle, Popeyes Louisiana Kitchen, and Momo N Curry. articles.title: BMW built the same car for gas and electric. The EV is $4,400 cheaper. | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The new BMW 3 Series shows just how quickly EVs have caught up to fossil fuel vehicles on pricing.
articles.body_text: For years, automotive analysts have been predicting that electric vehicles would become cheaper than their gas-powered equivalents. They figured it would happen sometime in the latter half of the 2020s. BloombergNEF , for example, expected it to happen in 2026. EV prices have dropped significantly in the last few years, but it has been hard to compare prices with fossil fuel vehicles because not every EV has a like-for-like gas-powered model. BMW has given us one. The 2027 BMW 3 Series comes in both gas and electric versions, and the EV is $4,400 cheaper . The gas-powered M350 xDrive will set you back $65,900, while the electric i3 50 xDrive will cost $61,500; neither price includes destination charges. Both are similarly powerful, similarly styled, and aimed at similar pocketbooks. The difference is the EV is 6.7% cheaper. Pedants will point out there’s a significantly cheaper gas-powered 3 Series trim, though it has no electric equivalent yet. The 2027 BMW 330 is priced at $49,900, and its upgraded xDrive trim costs $51,900. The two comparable vehicles are built on different platforms, with the EV i3 benefiting from BMW’s newest chassis and technology. The gas-powered 3 Series makes do with an overhauled version of an existing platform. For most people, the biggest difference will be the charging or refueling experience, but even there they’re more similar than some might expect. The range of the new gas 3 Series is likely similar to previous models, or about 450 miles per tank in all-wheel-drive guise. The electric i3 will travel 468 miles on a full charge, and BMW says the vehicle’s fast charging is speedy enough to replenish 208 miles of range in 10 minutes. The difference might be noticeable to extreme road warriors, but for most drivers, it’ll be academic. The generally accepted wisdom is that EVs have cost more up front, even if they’ve delivered a lower total cost of ownership . But now EVs are gaining the upper hand on purchase price, too. articles.title: The ugly economics of consumer AI | TechCrunch
articles.summary: There’s a reason frontier labs have gotten gun-shy about consumer AI — and it’s not because the tech isn’t good enough.
articles.body_text: After this week, you could argue that consumer AI is making a comeback. Meta’s personal AI assistant, Muse, and its plush-like mascot Jolly, has been a surprise hit . OpenAI’s Dots , released just yesterday, appears to be chasing the same cartoony personal assistant idea. And the up-and-coming Instinct assistant reached a $10 billion valuation on the strength of its agentic errand-running, focused on booking travel, making restaurant reservations, or cancelling subscriptions. The bull case is easy to make. Agentic AI has finally gotten reliable enough to handle everyday tasks. Companies are increasingly pitching that service to everyday people, who are getting genuine value out of it. If you’re an investor, that looks an awful lot like the ChatGPT launch in 2022 — the raw power of AI opening up a product category that was never possible before. Who wouldn’t want a piece of the action? But there’s a reason frontier labs have gotten gun-shy about consumer AI — and it’s not because the tech isn’t good enough. Even staggeringly popular tech products are starting to hit a ceiling on how much money consumers are willing to pay, and it’s not clear that better models are actually leading to a more profitable consumer business. The result has been an industry-wide shift toward the Anthropic model, focusing on enterprise contracts and vertical-by-vertical expansion. If products like Muse and Instinct are bucking that trend, it’s because they’re less concerned with monetization. But the underlying economics of consumer AI are not getting any better, and anyone getting into the business will have to grapple with them eventually. We got a reminder of those economics in Andreessen Horowitz’s semiannual State of Markets report , which pulled its figures from a PNC research report from this summer. In two charts, they track the slowly growing percentage of consumers paying for AI services, alongside the slowly growing amount they’re paying. As of May, 2.2% of consumers were paying for AI, at an average spend of $31 a month. Andreessen puts a positive spin on this, saying, “it’s still so early when it comes to mature AI adoption and utilization.” There’s a lot of room to grow! But in both charts, the pace of growth seems awfully linear. Even as models make huge improvements, there isn’t a ton of movement in the number of customers willing to pay for AI or how much they’re willing to pay for it. The enormous performance jump from GPT-5.2 to Astra, for instance, is barely visible on the chart. If you think PNC is underselling adoption, you can get similar numbers from Bank of America . In March, the firm found that roughly 3% of U.S. consumers paid for AI, up 40% from the previous year. A Menlo survey from September gives a slightly sunnier view, finding that a quarter of adults use AI daily and half of those users are paying for it. The problem with the consumer approach has less to do with revenue than with cost. AI is an unusually expensive technology to operate, particularly compared to lightweight predecessors like social networking or cloud computing. Even hundreds of millions of paying customers doesn’t guarantee you’ll break even. To its credit, OpenAI seems to have adapted well to these facts. The company’s widely reported pivot to enterprise has been largely successful, with enterprise bookings reportedly doubling since July. Even the Dots launch had a strong enterprise angle, showing how the new personal agent could be useful for software engineers and agency creatives. One long-standing way to make money from popular-but-cheap consumer services is to sell them to businesses at a markup, and OpenAI seems to be following the playbook. It’s harder to say what this means for Muse and Instinct. Muse has the juggernaut of Meta’s personalized ad targeting behind it, which gives it more options for monetization and more time before it becomes an urgent question. Notably, Meta is already exploring the enterprise angle . Instinct has a separate plan that involves taking a cut of purchases made through the agent, which might raise the ceiling. Presumably it’ll also be able to avoid the cost of training a frontier model, which will help a lot.

articles.title: CHATT: Vad undrar du om regeringskaoset?
articles.summary: Ställ dina frågor till Expressens politikreporter.
articles.body_text: Tack för alla fina frågor! Men nu måste jag stänga chatten för i dag och rusa vidare mot fortsatt politikbevakning här på Expressen. Om du inte fick svar denna gång så kommer snart en ny chans. Håll utkik! Vad som sker i ett extra val är det ingen som egentligen kan säga, vi har inga sådana erfarenheter i modern politisk tid. En del tror att den rödgröna sidan skulle straffas och högersidan stärkas. Andra att småpartier skulle kunna åka ur, och väljarna rösta på stora partier för att säkra en tydlig majoritet för en statsminister. Och så finns också risken att det blir ungefär samma låsta läge som nu. Personligen tror jag inte på partier som säger att de inte räds ett extra val. Det tror jag att alla gör. Inte minst för att det är omöjligt att sia om utgången och för att det är dyrt. Tror vi är många som förväntar oss ett högre tempo i regeringsbildningsprocessen nu än 2018. Det skulle inte förvåna mig heller om det kräver en rad snabba statsministeromröstningar. När vi börjar närma oss ett extra val kan det börja hända grejer, kanske luckras röda linjer upp då? Den som lever får se. I sak finns det förstås en möjlighet att bilda en regering av de partier som står mellan V och SD. Alltså MP, S, C, L, KD och M. I praktiken ser det svårare ut. Det var en sågning som heter duga! Jag tror mer om politiken. Just nu ser det väldigt tufft ut. Men en regering i någon form kommer Sverige att få. Med eller utan extra val (särskrivning av detta är ett påfund jag ogillar, men så ska det skrivas). Så klart ska vi i media, liksom politiken, ägna oss åt självrannsakan. Men jag delar inte bilden av att vi inte har försökt ge väljarna information. Vi har skrivit, poddat och sagt i tv hur många gånger som helst att det finns röda linjer som riskerar att försvåra en regeringsbildning på den rödgröna kanten. Men när vi har gjort det har vi anklagats för att ägna oss åt politiskt spel. Så jag delar inte uppfattningen om att vi inte har försökt. Vem som viker sig tror jag få vågar slå fast just nu. Men om det ska bli en rödgrön regering måste någon vika sig och ta en eventuell svekdebatt. Haha, ja kanske är det butiker som säljer popcorn som tjänar på krisen i regeringsbildningen? Ja, i landets kommuner och regioner ser vi en rad ovanliga konstellationer. Att det är mer låst på det nationella planet brukar förklaras med skillnaden i uppgifter. I kommuner är politiken mer hands-on, alltså den här skolan ska byggas och den här parkeringsplatsen måste bort, medan man i en regering sysslar med stora, övergripande frågor som rör lagar och landets ekonomi, vilket gör att partiernas ideologi väger tyngre. Oj, det är en 10 000 kronors fråga! Tror ingen i dag kan säga det. Väljarna har gett S, V, MP och C en knapp majoritet, så om partierna följer väljarnas vilja är det någon form av rödgrön regering som bildas. För att Ulf Kristersson ska få mandaten på sin sida måste han få stöd av fler partier än L, KD och SD. Just nu är det mycket låst. Det får vi ju se, han har inte mandatmatten på sin sida i detta nu. För att det ska gå måste något parti, kanske framför allt C, vara berett att ändra uppfattning. I nuläget talar ingenting för att C plötsligt skulle ändra uppfattning om SD. Många tycker att små partier har fått för stort inflytande på senare år. Men jag tror det är mycket långt borta, flera mandatperioder, innan en regering med S, M och SD ens är en möjlig lösning i teorin. Det finns alldeles för stora åsiktsskillnader mellan partierna. Däremot skulle en situation där Sverige hamnar i en mycket djup kris eller ett krig så klart kunna ändra på detta.

articles.summary: Åklagaren vill att den 31-åring som åtalats för misshandel av den svenska polisen Christian Zedig, som senare avled av skadorna, döms till fängelse.
articles.body_text: Åklagaren vill att den 31-åring som åtalats för misshandel av den svenska polisen Christian Zedig, som senare avled av skadorna, döms till fängelse. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Christian Zedig tilldelades enligt åtalet ett kraftigt knytnävsslag i samband med ett VM-arrangemang i Köpenhamn i juni. Slaget medförde bland annat att pulsådern brast och mannen avled tre dagar senare. Christian Zedig var anställd som polis i Sverige, men var inte i tjänst när misshandeln skedde vid ett storbildsevenemang på Islands Brygge under fotbolls-VM den 30 juni. Utöver fängelse anser åklagaren att den åtalade bör förbjudas att vistas på platser där det serveras alkohol nattetid, ett så kallat nattlivsförbud, visar handlingar som TT tagit del av. articles.body_text: Lotsen på fartyget inblandat i båtolyckan utanför Tjörn dömdes för vållande till annans död. Nu har lotsar i Marstrandområdet lagt ner arbetet, rapporterar GP. Ungefär tio fartyg i området kring Marstrand påverkas i nuläget av lotsarnas initiativ. Den tillförordnade chefen för lotsområdet, Ulf Eriksson, säger att lotsarna inte känner sig redo att arbeta efter att domen meddelats. – Domen väcker så många principiella frågor att man är osäker på om man kan fortsätta med det man håller på med, säger han. articles.body_text: 19-årige Gent Maksutaj blev ihjälskjuten under en kvällspromenad i Uppsala. Nu åtalas en 16-pojke för mordet, som enligt åklagaren rör sig om en felskjutning. – Hans primära mål har varit en annan person än den 19-åring som senare blir ihjälskjuten, säger åklagaren. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Den 5 juli i år sköts Gent Maksutaj, 19, ihjäl under en kvällspromenad på Kvarngärdet i Uppsala . Dagen efter greps en 16-årig pojke som misstänkt för mordet. Nu åtalas pojken för flera brott – mord, förberedelse till mord, grovt vapenbrott och brott mot lagen om brandfarliga och explosiva varor. Den mordmisstänkte pojken har erkänt, rapporterar UNT. Utredningen har visat att Gent Maksutaj inte var måltavla för dödsskjutningen. – Skytten har befunnit sig i Uppsala i flera dagar för att söka efter sitt tilltänkta offer, och att hans primära mål har varit en annan person än den 19-åring som senare blir ihjälskjuten, säger åklagare Mia Sjöstedt i ett pressmeddelande. – Vår teori är att gärningsmannen dirigerats till olika platser i Uppsala den 4–5 juli i syfte att göra så kallade provköp av narkotika i syfte att locka fram målsäganden. articles.title: Statsvetarna: Det är Kristerssons plan – när han får sondera • ”Samtal förs”
articles.summary: Ulf Kristersson (M) har sagt att Tidösamarbetet var ”ett projekt för förra mandatperioden”. Han kommer att undersöka möjligheten att bilda en minoritetsregering som får stöd av andra partier när han får sonderingsuppdraget, tror statsvetare. – Min gissning är att sådana diskussioner redan pågår, säger Jenny Madestam.
articles.body_text: Ulf Kristersson (M) har sagt att Tidösamarbetet var ”ett projekt för förra mandatperioden”. Han kommer att undersöka möjligheten att bilda en minoritetsregering som får stöd av andra partier när han får sonderingsuppdraget, tror statsvetare. – Min gissning är att sådana diskussioner redan pågår, säger Jenny Madestam. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Statsvetarna Andreas Johansson Heinö och Jenny Madestam tror att Socialdemokraternas ledare Magdalena Andersson snart får tillbaka sonderingsuppdraget av talmannen och att hon kommer att förlora den första statsministeromröstningen. De tror också att Moderaternas ledare Ulf Kristersson får nästa möjlighet att sondera förutsättningarna för att bilda en ny regering. Efter riksdagsvalet har Kristersson flera gånger sagt att det finns en ”icke-socialistisk” majoritet i riksdagen och att ”några röda linjer måste flyttas, annars får vi ingen regering”. Förra veckan sa han till Dagens industri att Tidösamarbetet ”alldeles entydigt” var ”ett projekt för förra mandatperioden”. Vad kommer M-ledaren att göra när han får sonderingsuppdraget? Jenny Madestam tror att Kristersson kommer att undersöka möjligheten att bilda en minoritetsregering som får stöd av andra partier, inklusive Sverigedemokraterna och Centerpartiet. – Absolut. Min gissning är att sådana diskussioner redan pågår. Jag tror att det är samtal som förs, inte på partiledarnivå men på en nivå längre ner. – Det skulle väl vara hans alternativ. Någon typ av minoritetsregering med stöd av Centerpartiet och Sverigedemokraterna. Hon tror att samtal förs mellan framför allt Moderaterna och Centerpartiet, men kanske även med Kristdemokraterna och Liberalerna.

articles.title: Chaufförens chock: Ohygglig upplevelse
articles.summary: Skadorna på Strömsundsbron kommer ta ”en längre tid” att laga. En månad, enligt Trafikverkets prognos. Ännu längre, tror professorn John Leander.
articles.body_text: Skadorna på Strömsundsbron kommer ta ”en längre tid” att laga. Ännu längre, tror professorn John Leander. – Broar klarar normalt sett inte så här stora deformationer, säger han till ÖP. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Strax innan midnatt i tisdags gick Strömsundsbron vid E45 sönder. Ett tungt transportfordon, som väger nästan 100 ton, försökte köra över bron. I slutet av färden märkte föraren att bron rest sig nästan en halvmeter. Bron spärrades genast av och räddningstjänst, polis och Trafikverket åkte till platsen. Trafikverket meddelade att bron kommer vara avstängd under en ”längre tid”, och satte en första preliminär prognos på en månad. Man flaggar dock för att det kan ta både kortare och längre tid än så. – Det man gör i dag är att försöka få bort den här transporten. Först då kan man börja arbeta på bron och försöka analysera vad det är som behöver åtgärdas, sa kommunikatör Daniel Mossberg på onsdagen. Att reparera skadorna lär dock bli svårt, tror professor John Leander vid KTH. Hans forskning är särskilt inriktad på just brokonstruktioner. – Att resa sig på det sättet kan ha fått följdverkningar som är svåra att se och svåra att återställa, säger han till Östersunds-Posten. Fordonet hade fått dispens av Trafikverket att köra över, trots att det vägde mer än de 74 ton som bron har bärighetsklassning för. Bärighetsklassen innebär dock att bron ska klara av flera fordon på 74 ton samtidigt. – Det här är en erfaren chaufför. Allt tyder på att allt är gjort helt korrekt av det vi kan se hittills, både med transport och vikter och allt, säger Tom Brede Johansen, vice vd på företaget som körde transporten, till ÖP. Det var en obehaglig upplevelse för chauffören, säger hans chef Espen Johnsen till SVT Jämtland.

articles.title: General Gadi Eisenkot kan besegra Netanyahu i Israels val
articles.summary: General Gadi Eisenkot kan besegra Netanyahu i Israels val
articles.body_text: Han är mannen som kan bli Israels näste premiärminister. Den gamle generalen Gadi Eisenkot har goda chanser att besegra Benjamin Netanyahu i valet i slutet av oktober. – Det är ett ödesdigert val, regeringen förstör landet, säger förstagångsväljaren Alma Silber på ett valmöte med Eisenkot i Kiryat Gat i södra Israel. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Den politiska temperaturen ökar i Israel inför valet till parlamentet, Knesset. Ett val som många, både till höger och vänster, beskriver som ”ödesdigert”. Deltagarna jublar när Gadi Eisenkot, tidigare överbefälhavare, kommer in på sitt valmöte i staden Kiryat Gat i södra Israel på tisdagskvällen. – Här kommer Israels nästa premiärminister! ropar speakern och den gamle generalen får stående applåder. Gadi Eisenkot, tidigare ÖB, kan bli Israels näste premiärminister Han har god chans att besegra Benjamin Netanyahu i valet i slutet av oktober. ”Det är ett ödesdigert val”, säger förstagångsväljaren Alma Silber, 18, på ett valmöte i Kiryat Gat i södra Israel Israel är ett politiskt djupt splittrat land och många pekar ut premiärminister Benjamin Netanyahu som främst ansvarig för polariseringen. Hans nuvarande koalition med extrema högerpartier ligger något efter i de ofta otillförlitliga mätningarna – och en bred mitten/vänsteropinion hoppas på regeringsskifte efter hans sammanlagt 19 år vid makten. Många har försökt besegra Netanyahu, 76, genom åren, men misslyckats. Nu står oppositionens hopp till före detta överbefälhavaren Gadi Eisenkot, 66, en relativ nykomling i politiken.
